title: Phillies-Giants trade grades: Luis Arraez move could boost Philadelphia’s lineup
content:
The Athletic has live coverage of the 2026 MLB Trade Deadline.

Giants get: RHP Ramon Marquez, RHP Marty Gair

Phillies get: INF Luis Arraez, RHP Caleb Kilian

Giants: B
Phillies: A

The Phillies needed an infusion of talent, and Arraez provides some diversity for their lineup. His contact-based approach will aid a lineup built around sluggers hitting .250. The Phillies will also have to hope that his recent defensive improvement can continue without the daily tutelage of infield guru Ron Washington. But it’s an obviously useful addition for a team that still believes it can win a title in 2026.

As for the Giants, the success of this deal may depend on Marquez’s ability to fool hitters with his changeup as he rises through the minor-league ranks. Both Marquez and Gair have been pitching for Class-A Jersey Shore. Gair is already a reliever. Marquez may become one. But he has posted some absurd strikeout numbers, 14.2 per nine innings, against lower-level competition. The changeup may be enough to carry him to the majors as a solid reliever if he can’t stick in the rotation. — Andy McCullough

Giants: B+
Phillies: A

Did you really think Dave Dombrowski wasn’t going to trade for an infielder? Did Bryce Harper honestly believe Dealer Dave needed a nudge in that direction? Come on, now. The Phillies’ infield has been a mess for months, and their lineup has sorely lacked an on-base threat at the top of the order. Arraez addresses those issues as well as any readily available player on the market. The Phillies will have to restructure their infield a bit to make him fit, but that should be the least of their worries. They’re among the worst in baseball in batting average and on-base percentage, and they just traded for a batting champ with a .360 OBP.

It doesn’t solve every Phillies problem — the outfield still needs help — but it’s a step in the right direction for a team that’s firmly in win-now mode. Bonus points for also getting a controllable reliever in the deal. Marquez is a tough player to lose, but by the time he’s fully formed, the Phillies could be in their rebuilding phase. Dombrowski cashed in that tantalizing-but-uncertain future for a piece he badly needed here and now. A predictable and productive move by an executive always motivated to win. — Chad Jennings
